name: Wish Poosh Campground
note: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF (Cle Elum Ranger District) campground near the SE shore of Cle Elum Lake, ~10 mi NW of Cle Elum off WA-903. 34 sites for tents/RVs, no hookups, vault toilets and drinking water; RVs to ~45 ft. Mix of reservable and first-come, first-served sites (reservable online). --Claude

name: Chatter Creek Campground
note: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF (Wenatchee River Ranger District) at the confluence of Icicle Creek and Chatter Creek, ~16 mi up Icicle Creek Rd (FR7600) from Leavenworth. 12 single sites first-come, first-served (plus 1 reservable group site); vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups; RVs to ~22 ft. Open roughly late May-early Oct. --Claude

name: Fox Creek Campground
note: USFS Okanogan-Wenatchee (Entiat RD) campground, 16 shaded drive-in sites along the Entiat River (~27 mi up Entiat River Rd), no hookups, max trailer 28 ft, ~2,000 ft; scan-and-pay/FCFS via the recreation.gov app, open mid-May to late Oct. --Claude

name: Lake Creek Campground (Entiat River)
note: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF, Entiat Ranger District, ~27 mi up Entiat River Road along the Entiat River at ~2,200 ft. 18 sites (tent/RV, no hookups), max trailer ~25 ft; vault toilets, no potable water. 9 sites reservable online, 9 FCFS. --Claude

name: Hunters Campground (Lake Roosevelt NRA)
note: NPS Lake Roosevelt NRA campground on the Columbia (Lake Roosevelt); 37 reservable drive-in sites, no hookups, RVs to 60 ft, flush toilets and seasonal drinking water, boat launch and beach on site. Reservation-only, no FCFS. Reservable online. No cell service. --Claude

name: Clear Creek Campground (Darrington)
note: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF campground 3 mi south of Darrington on the Mountain Loop Highway, on Clear Creek near the Sauk River; 13 drive-in sites, RVs to 40 ft, no hookups, no drinking water, vault toilets. Reservable online with some FCFS availability. --Claude

name: Horseshoe Cove Campground
note: USFS (Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF, Mt. Baker RD) campground on the west shore of Baker Lake. ~40 sites (35 single, 2 double, 1 group), no hookups, flush toilets, potable water, boat ramp and large sandy swim beach; several sites at the lake's edge. Reservable online (some FCFS). Open May-Sep. --Claude

name: Panorama Point Campground
note: USFS (Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF) campground on the western shore of Baker Lake, ~19 mi up Baker Lake Rd (FR 11). 14 sites (11 single, 3 double), RVs to ~35 ft, no hose hookups (fill elsewhere), drinking water, vault toilets. Reservable online (1 FCFS). Open May-Sep. --Claude

name: Early Winters Campground
note: USFS (Okanogan-Wenatchee NF, Methow Valley RD) campground ~15 mi W of Winthrop on Hwy 20 along Early Winters Creek near its Methow River confluence. 12 sites in a north and south loop (south loop handles RV/trailer traffic, open pine forest), no hookups, potable water, vault toilets. First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay via Recreation.gov app on site). Open ~Apr-Nov. --Claude

name: South Creek Campground
note: Small USFS drive-in campground at the confluence of South Creek and the Twisp River, ~22 mi W of Twisp via Twisp River Rd/FR 44 then gravel FR 4440 (Okanogan-Wenatchee NF, Methow Valley RD). No hookups, no potable water, vault toilet; sites accommodate RVs up to 30 ft. First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay). --Claude

name: Meadows Campground
note: High-alpine USFS campground (~6,250 ft) near Harts Pass, ~20 mi NW of Mazama via gravel Harts Pass Rd (FR 5400) then FR 5400-500 (Okanogan-Wenatchee NF). Access road is narrow with steep cliffs and NO TRAILERS are allowed (FR 5400 closed to trailers Jun 1-Dec 31); small self-contained motorhomes only. FS lists '1 RV and 1 tent max per site'; no hookups, no potable water, vault toilet. First-come, first-served, typically open Jul-Sep. --Claude

name: Nice Campground
note: Small 3-site USFS drive-in campground along Eightmile Creek on paved Eightmile Rd (FR 5130), ~11 mi N of Winthrop (Okanogan-Wenatchee NF); burned in the 2021 Cub Creek fire, now open/sunny. No hookups, no potable water, vault toilet; sites reported to fit RVs to ~36 ft (34 ft reported). First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay). --Claude

name: River Bend Campground
note: USFS drive-in campground on the upper Methow River near Mazama, ~24 mi NW of Winthrop via Lost River Rd then gravel Harts Pass Rd (FR 5400) ~1.75 mi in (Okanogan-Wenatchee NF). RVs up to 28 ft (one pull-through, several back-ins); no hookups, no potable water, vault toilet. River a ~30-sec walk from sites. First-come, first-served, open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Mystery Campground
note: Small forested first-come, first-served Forest Service campground along the Twisp River ~18.5 mi NW of Twisp (Twisp River Rd/County Rd 9114 to FR 44 to gravel FR 4440); some sites to 30 ft, vault toilets, no potable water, pack out trash. On-site Scan-and-Pay via the rec.gov app. --Claude

name: Poplar Flat Campground
note: First-come, first-served Forest Service campground on the Twisp River ~21 mi NW of Twisp (Twisp River Rd to FR 44 to gravel FR 4440); 16 sites, max RV 30 ft, potable water, vault toilets, community kitchen shelter. On-site Scan-and-Pay via rec.gov. --Claude

name: Ruffed Grouse Campground
note: Small (6-site) first-come, first-served Forest Service campground along Eightmile Creek ~15 mi NW of Winthrop (W Chewuch Rd/CR 1213 to Eightmile Rd/FR 5130); RV limit 35 ft, no hookups, vault toilet, no potable water, pack out trash. --Claude

name: Ballard Campground
note: Small rustic first-come, first-served Forest Service campground along the West Fork Methow River near Mazama, ~9 mi up Lost River Rd + gravel FR 5400; ~7 sites including a pull-through fitting RVs to 35 ft, vault toilet, no potable water. On-site Scan-and-Pay via rec.gov. --Claude

name: Blackpine Lake Campground
note: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF (Methow Valley RD) drive-in campground on Blackpine (Black Pine) Lake at ~4,000 ft, reached via paved Twisp River Rd then FR 43 (the Poorman Creek route is too narrow for trailers). 14 tent/RV sites up to 30 ft, vault toilets, potable water, no hookups; boat launch and docks for non-motorized boats. First-come, first-served (on-site Scan & Pay). --Claude

name: Buck Lake Campground
note: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF (Methow Valley RD) small campground on Buck Lake north of Winthrop, reached via W Chewuch Rd to Eightmile Creek Rd (FR 5130) then Buck Lake Rd (FR 5130-100). 9 sites, max RV length 25 ft, vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups; 14-night limit. First-come, first-served (on-site Scan & Pay). --Claude

name: Chewuch Campground
note: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF (Methow Valley RD) campground in ponderosa pine along the Chewuch River, ~15 mi north of Winthrop on paved FR 51, ~2,300 ft. 16 sites, max RV length 35 ft, potable water (hand pump), vault toilets, no hookups. First-come, first-served (on-site Scan & Pay). --Claude

name: Foggy Dew Campground
note: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF (Methow Valley RD) small campground at the confluence of Foggy Dew Creek and North Fork Gold Creek, ~11 mi from Carlton, ~2,100 ft. 11 sites, max RV length 25 ft, vault toilets, no potable water, no hookups; trailhead access for hiking/mountain biking. First-come, first-served (on-site Scan & Pay). --Claude

name: Loup Loup Campground
note: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF (Methow Valley RD), ~4,200 ft on Loup Loup summit off Hwy 20 near Twisp. 25 meadow/lightly-forested sites, no hookups, vault toilets, potable water; some sites fit RVs to ~34 ft. First-come, first-served (Scan & Pay). --Claude

name: Bonaparte Lake Campground
note: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF (Tonasket RD), ~3,600 ft on the south end of Bonaparte Lake east of Tonasket. 33 individual/family sites plus 1 group site; flush toilets, potable water, boat launch, accessible fishing dock; no hookups; some sites accommodate RVs to ~32 ft. Some sites reservable online, single/double sites also FCFS; open ~May 15-Oct 17. --Claude

name: Salmon Meadows
note: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF (Tonasket RD), ~4,400 ft in a large meadow north of Conconully. 14 sites, vault toilets, no hookups; some sites accommodate RVs/trailers to ~32 ft. First-come, first-served, ~$10/night, open ~May 15-Oct 15. --Claude

name: Swan Lake Campground
note: Colville NF campground on Swan Lake, ~14 mi SW of Republic via WA-21 and paved FR 53 (Scatter Creek). 26 sites (incl 4 walk-in tent sites) in a mixed-pine setting; the lakeshore loop accommodates moderate-size trailers/RVs with lake views and the non-lakeshore loop holds the pull-through sites. Potable water, vault toilets, no hookups. First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay). --Claude

name: Cottonwood Campground (Tonasket RD)
note: Small Okanogan-Wenatchee NF (Tonasket RD) campground on North Fork Salmon Creek, off FR 38 just north of Conconully. 3 single sites plus 1 group camp; each site has a picnic table, fire ring, and parking spur; artesian-well water, vault toilet, no hookups. Takes tents and RVs. First-come, first-served, $8. --Claude

name: Kerr Campground
note: Okanogan-Wenatchee NF (Tonasket RD) campground on North Fork Salmon Creek, ~2 mi north of Conconully via County Rd 2361/FR 38. Two loops, 12 sites (11 single, 1 double); picnic table, fire ring, vault toilets; no potable water, no hookups, no dump. First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay), open ~May 1-Oct 27. --Claude

name: Deer Creek Forest Camp
note: Colville NF forest camp at the summit on the Deer Creek Hwy near the Kettle Crest Trail #13 and PNT; 6 drive-in sites (mix of back-in and pull-through, level parking spurs ~50-60 ft), horse corrals, one vault toilet, no drinking water. Reconstructed after the 2015 Stickpin Fire. Fee, first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Beacon Rock State Park (Woodard Creek Campground)
note: WA State Park in the Columbia River Gorge. Woodard Creek Campground has 2 standard and 5 full-hookup drive-in sites (RVs/combos to 40 ft), reservable online, sited near SR-14 and the BNSF tracks (train noise). Park also has a 26-site FCFS upper campground plus group and equestrian camps and 9,500 ft of Columbia River shoreline. --Claude

name: Grayland Beach State Park
note: Pacific coast WA State Park on the Long Beach-area shore south of Westport; large paved back-in/pull-through sites (primitive through full-hookup) with pads accommodating rigs up to 60 ft (limited), plus yurts. Reservable through Washington State Parks (washington.goingtocamp.com); ~50 sites are FCFS Nov 1-Apr 15 due to seasonal flooding. Five trails cross the dunes to the beach. --Claude

name: Sahara Creek Horse Camp
note: WA DNR camp in the Elbe Hills/Tahoma State Forest off SR-706 near Ashford. Gravel drive-in sites (majority equestrian but open to general camping), large sites with room for most RVs, vault toilets, no water or hookups, pack-in/pack-out. First-come, first-served (Discover Pass required); email reservation option except holiday weekends. --Claude

name: Bear Creek Campground
note: WA DNR recreation campground on the Sol Duc River, just off US 101 near Sappho/Beaver. 14 sites on a one-way gravel loop with several pull-throughs fitting RVs to ~30 ft; picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets, no potable water. First-come, first-served (Discover Pass required). Site 8 has a Sol Duc River view deck. --Claude

name: Sequim Bay State Park
note: WA State Parks campground on Sequim Bay near Sequim. Standard and full-utility drive-in sites; RVs/combinations to 40 ft. Reservable May 15-Sep 15, first-come first-served off-season. Restrooms w/ showers. Note: park scheduled closed Jun 5-Sep 15, 2026 for new-entrance construction, then reopens. Reservable online. --Claude Rechecked 2026-09-30: park open; only the Lower Loop is closed (Aug 30, 2026-Jan 30, 2027) for restroom construction. --Claude

name: Jarrell Cove State Park
note: WA State Parks on Harstine Island's Jarrell Cove (Pickering Passage). Small campground: 10 standard + 2 partial-hookup drive-in sites + 1 marine-trail site; sites 5-7 FCFS, the rest reservable, no dump station. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Teanaway Campground
note: WA DNR campground in the Teanaway Community Forest along the West Fork Teanaway River. 55 sites: drive-in sites for trailers/RVs up to ~25 ft plus walk-in tent sites; pit toilets, fire rings, picnic tables; no hookups, no potable water, no trash service. First-come, first-served (Discover Pass required). --Claude

name: Bridgeport Bar Wildlife Area (WDFW)
note: WDFW wildlife-area unit on the south side of the Columbia River (Rufus Woods Lake) east of Brewster; primitive drive-in camping/overnight parking allowed in established gravel access areas with a concrete boat launch and restroom - no developed/marked sites, no open fires year-round, Discover Pass required, first-come first-served. --Claude

name: Coffeepot Lake Recreation Site
note: BLM (Spokane District) recreation site on Coffeepot Lake in the channeled scablands SW of Harrington; 7 first-come first-served drive-in sites with picnic table and fire ring, vault toilet, graveled boat launch and fishing dock, no potable water (pack it in/out). Access road is steep gravel - about 5 sites fit smaller trailers/truck campers to ~23 ft; not recommended for large rigs. --Claude

name: Twin Lakes Recreation Area (BLM)
note: BLM-managed primitive recreation area at Upper/Lower Twin Lake near Davenport/Harrington. Several drive-in dispersed sites - a couple before the lakes and the rest along the shore; no hookups, vault toilet, primitive boat launches. Access is ~2 mi of narrow dirt/gravel/rocky road off Highline Rd - passable but tight, best for small/medium rigs (RV-suitable pull-offs near the top). First-come, first-served, no BLM fee; Discover Pass reportedly required. --Claude

name: Birch Bay State Park
note: Large forested state park on Birch Bay (saltwater). ~147 standard drive-in sites plus 20 partial-hookup and 2 primitive across North/South loops; RVs/combos to ~40-60 ft, dump station, showers. Reservable online; North Loop (sites 1-38) is first-come, first-served Sept 16-May 14. --Claude

name: Curlew Lake State Park
note: WA State Parks campground on the east shore of Curlew Lake near Republic. Standard, partial- and full-hookup drive-in sites including 6 pull-throughs, max site length 45 ft, one dump station; sites 73-80 have a no-fee mooring dock. Mostly reservable, a few FCFS. --Claude
